@copilot Update this PR directly to finish the mechanism-neutral Javadocs explicitly requested in the original assignment. Delivery inspection of head 051d3cf402819a5963f66ebf6dbf3ee891dfb52d confirms the 22 public method renames and caller migrations, but the original method descriptions were left unchanged.

Examples of the remaining mismatch: JavaHttpClientTelemetry.instrument still says "Returns a new instrumented HttpClient that wraps the provided client"; OpenAITelemetry.instrument and ThriftTelemetry.instrumentClient/instrumentAsyncClient still begin "Wraps"; AwsSdkTelemetry's methods still promise construction of a new instance and its class Javadoc still requires "wrapping"; CassandraTelemetry's first instrument overload still promises a new session and returns the concrete TracingCqlSession in its Javadoc; KafkaTelemetry describes decorated producers/consumers; RocketMqTelemetry describes a decorated producer and "before wrapping it". JdbcTelemetry.instrument and R2dbcTelemetry.instrumentConnectionFactory have no method Javadoc.

Use concise descriptions such as "Returns an instrumented {@link HttpClient} based on the supplied client", with appropriate nouns for the renamed entrypoints. Update related class/usage descriptions only where they define these public entrypoints in terms of wrapping. Preserve useful configuration, contact-point, server/client protocol, telemetry, and resource-ownership requirements. Keep RocketMQ's configure-before-instrumenting and returned-producer/batch-send instructions without presenting wrapping as the API contract. Do not add disclaimers about original mutation, instance identity, or a required wrapping/copying mechanism. Already mechanism-neutral descriptions can stay unchanged.

This is the omitted documentation portion of the agreed naming migration, not a production refactor. Do not rename internal helpers or test abstractions, change implementations, add aliases, redesign overloads, or alter Ratpack/WebFlux. Apply narrow formatting and the applicable repository Markdown linter only if Markdown changes; documentation-only edits do not need new behavioral tests. Preserve this PR as a draft. The coordinator handles its title and description.

Also address the verified finding from Copilot review 5688734881, comment 4405323619: move this PR's wrap*/instrument* rename changelog entry from the stable "Breaking changes" section into the existing "Breaking changes to non-stable APIs" section. version.gradle.kts uses the alpha version unless otel.stable=true, and none of these library modules opts into stability. Preserve the wording and all unrelated entries. Do not reply to or resolve the review thread; the coordinator will verify the fix and handle that thread.

@copilot Update this PR directly to follow the naming guidance in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/21052. Public telemetry methods that instrument an existing library object should use instrument(...) overloads when parameter types distinguish operations and are available together on supported consumer compile classpaths. This request supersedes the earlier instruction to preserve all method suffixes.

Rename IcebergTelemetry.instrumentScan(Scan<T1,T2,T3>) to instrument(...), and R2dbcTelemetry.instrumentConnectionFactory(ConnectionFactory, ConnectionFactoryOptions) to instrument(...).

In ThriftTelemetry, rename instrumentClient(TServiceClient, Class<T>), instrumentAsyncClient(TAsyncClient, Class<T>), instrumentServerProcessor(TProcessor, String), and instrumentClientProtocol(TProtocol) to instrument(...) overloads. Their parameter types are distinct and come from the same libthrift dependency.

Preserve the justified exceptions. Keep AwsSdkTelemetry.instrumentBedrockRuntimeClient separate from the SQS instrument overloads because Bedrock is an optional dependency. Keep ThriftTelemetry.instrumentServerInProtocolFactory, instrumentServerOutProtocolFactory, and instrumentClientProtocolFactory distinct because all three accept TProtocolFactory but serve different roles. Leave other correctly named instrument overloads unchanged.

Update all affected production callers, Javaagent and Spring integrations, tests, Javadocs, and README usage examples consistently. Preserve generic types, signatures apart from the method names, runtime behavior, existing mechanism-neutral documentation, and the breaking-rename policy without deprecated aliases. Do not rename internal wrapping helpers or introduce unrelated API changes. Apply narrowly scoped formatting and the repository Markdown linter for any changed Markdown, then run relevant targeted tests for the affected modules and callers. Preserve this PR's draft state. Acceptance criteria: no obsolete public method names or stale calls/examples for the six methods above remain; overloads compile with supported dependencies; all intentional exceptions remain unchanged.

@copilot Finish all remaining naming changes in this PR to follow https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/21052. The previous attempt ended successfully but commit 3270c36db105dbb560099c9b4bd4266addd2e8cd changed only Iceberg. Delivery inspection confirms the following five requested public renames are still missing. This assignment covers both R2DBC and Thrift plus their callers and documentation, not just the inline anchor. Complete all five renames in this attempt.

In instrumentation/r2dbc-1.0/library, rename R2dbcTelemetry.instrumentConnectionFactory(ConnectionFactory, ConnectionFactoryOptions) to instrument(ConnectionFactory, ConnectionFactoryOptions). Update all references, including R2dbcInstrumentation in the Javaagent module, R2dbcInstrumentingPostProcessor in Spring autoconfigure, library tests, and README examples.

In instrumentation/thrift-0.13/library, rename these four ThriftTelemetry methods to instrument(...) overloads: instrumentClient(TServiceClient, Class<T>), instrumentAsyncClient(TAsyncClient, Class<T>), instrumentServerProcessor(TProcessor, String), and instrumentClientProtocol(TProtocol). Update every affected Thrift test, README example and Javadoc reference. Their parameter types are distinct and available together from libthrift, so these methods do not qualify for distinct-name exceptions.

Preserve ThriftTelemetry.instrumentServerInProtocolFactory, instrumentServerOutProtocolFactory, and instrumentClientProtocolFactory as separate names because all accept TProtocolFactory but serve different roles. Preserve AwsSdkTelemetry.instrumentBedrockRuntimeClient because Bedrock is an optional dependency. Leave the already-correct Iceberg instrument method and other instrument overloads unchanged. Preserve signatures apart from the method names, generic types, runtime behavior, mechanism-neutral documentation, and the breaking-rename policy without deprecated aliases. Do not rename internal wrapping helpers or add unrelated API changes.

Also clarify the existing non-stable-API changelog entry in response to Copilot review 5689616353, comment 4406021566. Keep it concise, for example: Rename public library wrap/wrapXxx entrypoints to instrument overloads, retaining distinct instrumentXxx names where required. Keep Markdown code formatting around method names and preserve unrelated changelog entries. Do not reply to or resolve review threads.

Apply the narrow formatting tasks and repository Markdown linter for changed Markdown, then run relevant targeted tests for both affected modules and callers. Preserve this PR as a draft. Acceptance criteria: all five public methods above are named instrument, no stale references to their old public names remain, all intentional exceptions are preserved, and all related callers/examples are consistent. Update this existing PR directly and do not stop after changing only the anchored method.
